content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper is the following work of [Fang et al., NeurIPS, 2021]. The authors proposed a logic spiking network(LSN) based on excitatory pathways and inhibitory pathways to overcome the non-binary output of SEW ADD ResNet. The authors test the performance on CIFAR10, ImageNet, and the neuromorphic dataset CIFAR10-DVS.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
1. The results are unreliable. This paper revised the work of [Fang et al., NeurIPS, 2021] by adding another pathway. We have reproduced the experiments by Spikingjelly. We find that the proposed network cannot improve performance. The authors should upload the code instead of the model. The author should be cautious about this problem!

I did a further analysis of the gradient. I noticed that the logical operation in LSN will lose many gradient information. For example, if ${\cal E}=0, {\cal I}=1, {\cal X}_l=0$, the gradients $\frac{\partial {\cal X}_l+1}{\partial {\cal E}}$, $\frac{\partial {\cal X}_l+1}{\partial {\cal I}}$, $\frac{\partial {\cal X}_l+1}{\partial {\cal X}_l}$ are all zero. Another example, if ${\cal E}=1, {\cal I}=0, {\cal X}_l=1$, the gradients $\frac{\partial {\cal X}_l+1}{\partial {\cal E}}$, $\frac{\partial {\cal X}_l+1}{\partial {\cal I}}$, $\frac{\partial {\cal X}_l+1}{\partial {\cal X}_l}$ are all zero as well. I summarized all the cases of gradients in the following Table. We can find that the gradient is not 0 in only half of the cases, which will result in a significant loss of gradient information. I doubt this will lead to the non-convergence of the algorithm. Please analyze the impact of the loss of gradient information. Please give proof of the convergence of LSN.

| 0            | 1          | 1          | 1                                                     | 0                                                   | -1                                                  |

2. The authors over-claimed the contribution of their work. The authors claim they are the first to train an SNN with binary output and more than 100 layers. In fact, the work of [Fang et al., NeurIPS, 21] has trained SEW IAND ResNet-152 network and the output are binary spikes. Please refer to section 4.1 and Figure 5 of [Fang et al., NeurIPS, 21].

3. The authors are not familiar with the research progress of SNNs. In related works, they ignore many important papers in recent two years. For example, ANN2SNN [1-4] and Surrogate Gradient [5-6].

[1] Li, Y., Deng, S., Dong, X., Gong, R., & Gu, S. (2021). A free lunch from ANN: Towards efficient, accurate spiking neural networks calibration. ICML

[2] Meng, Q, et al. Training much deeper spiking neural networks with a small number of time-steps. Neural Networks 153 (2022): 254-268.

[3] Bu, T., Fang, W., Ding, J., Dai, P., Yu, Z., & Huang, T. (2022). Optimal ANN-SNN Conversion for High-accuracy and Ultra-low-latency Spiking Neural Networks. ICLR.

[4] Wang, Y., et al. (2022) Signed Neuron with Memory: Towards Simple, Accurate and High-Efficient ANN-SNN Conversion. IJCAI.2022.

[5] Meng, Q., Xiao, M., Yan, S., Wang, Y., Lin, Z., & Luo, Z. Q. (2022). Training High-Performance Low-Latency Spiking Neural Networks by Differentiation on Spike Representation. CVPR.

[6] Kim, Y., & Panda, P. (2021). Optimizing deeper spiking neural networks for dynamic vision sensing. Neural Networks, 144, 686-698.

4. This paper is riddled with typos and grammatical mistakes. The authors should rewrite the paper.

display_title: Our experiments are reproducible, and we have experimentally and theoretically proved that LSN does not have the problem of gradient vanishing.

content.title: Our experiments are reproducible, and we have experimentally and theoretically proved that LSN does not have the problem of gradient vanishing.
content.comment:
**The results are reliable**  
We can ensure that all experiments are reproducible, we re-upload the training code and model code on different datasets and the original recording of the training process. And our pre-trained models are released at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1sg0faf4a9bO10I4af3jaOx7lRAtH8CSL?usp=sharing.  

**LSN does not have the problem of gradient vanishing**  
Regarding the gradient problem, first of all, thank you very much for your further theoretical derivation. Some cases where the gradient is 0 in the truth table caused by the logical operation will not cause the network to lose the gradient.  
+ (i) For the ReLU activation function often used in ANN, when the input is less than 0, the gradient during backpropagation is also 0, and when the output is greater than 0, the gradient is always 1, which does not cause the problem of gradient disappearance, but makes ReLU enable the network to converge faster than other activation functions. During the back-propagation of logical operations in LSN, the gradient of 0 in some cases is consistent with ReLU, and it does not cause the problem of gradient vanishing.  
+ (ii) This bitwise multiplication method has been used in the Highway Network(https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.00387). The forward propagation process of LSN can be regarded as the application of a gating mechanism. In the forward propagation process of the Highway network, the output of the branch is multiplied by the value of the sigmoid output, and the value output of the sigmoid is between 0 and 1. The original paper discusses two extreme cases, that is, the gate value output is 0 or 1. , and the process of LSN forward propagation can be written in the form of a gating mechanism with the output of gating is 0 or 1, so LSN also does not have the problem of gradient vanishing.  
+ (iii) We visualized the gradients during the fifth epoch of training on the CIFAR10 dataset. It is proved that it solves the problem of gradient disappearance compared with Spiking ResNet, and the gradient during LSN backpropagation remains stable between the deep and shallow layers of the network. We made additions in Appendix A.2.

**Our contribution**  
We claim we are the first to train an SNN with binary output and more than 100 layers mainly means that LSN can achieve competitive results with binary output on complex datasets such as ImageNet and is more brain-like. The output of the SEW IAND network cannot be changed from 1 to 0, which limits the fitting ability of the network. The performance of SEW IAND on complex datasets is far lower than that of the SEW ADD, which loses the benefits brought by the deepening of the network. It is biologically equivalent to the spike that will not fire again as long as it disappears, which is inconsistent with the biological mechanism. And LSN can convert 0/1 in a more brain-like way.

**Finally, we re-emphasize that all our experiments are reliable and we have resubmitted the code and original training records as supplementary material, our pretrained model also can be available.**

Our article has a lot of room for revision, so we choose to withdraw it.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: Authors propose a spiking neural network by introducing a neuron model with binary outputs such that the network may be extended to higher levels of deepness, reaching more than 100 layers. This is accomplished by defining a neuron model which incorporates a logical operation between its input and a pair of excitatory and inhibitory pathways. Quantitative results show a very positive trade-off between accuracy and the number of parameters.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
A strength of the paper is the innovative aspects of the neuron model and its efficiency in overcoming the vanishing gradient problem. This leads to quantitatively better results compared to other SNN architectures (yet, as is expected, at lower levels than the generic SOTA). Another novelty of the paper is to incorporate Excitatory and Inhibitory pathways in a local neural circuitry. 

A weakness is that this auxiliary novelty is not fully studied. Indeed, how have you determined the look-up table in Table 2? How do your relate this binary operation to the continuous effects of biological excitatory or inhibitory conductances? How does these pathways contribute to your quantitative results?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clearly written and brings all necessary elements in the text with the right amount of details.
content.summary_of_the_review: In summary, the proposed algorithm is clearly novel and provides with a clear advantage over other SNN architectures which would clearly benefit to the community. To alleviate the weakness regarding the role of the local circuitry, the paper would benefit from an additional control highlighting the benefit of these pathways and of the interactions defined in Table 2.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes the LSN, Logical Spiking Networks, to study how to prolong the networks and increase SNN's performance. Starting with the original ResNet, this paper analyzes the 5 variants of residual connections. Then this paper proposes a method to divide one layer into two, namely excitatory and inhibitory pathways. Then, the authors combined two features with logical operations.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The advantages and disadvantages can be summarized here:

**advantages**: 

+ This paper studies the residual connection problem in SNN, precisely pointing out the flaw of existing methods, (although the full pre-activation analysis may be wrong). 

+ This paper outline the thought trajectory of this problem.

**disadvantages**:

- The analysis of full pre-activation may be wrong, i.e. Figure 2(e). See full implementation in [BiT's implementation on ResNet50v2](https://github.com/google-research/big_transfer/blob/master/bit_pytorch/models.py), which has a ReLU at the end of all residual blocks. In SNN, this ReLU ought to be LIF to ensure the final output is binarized. 

- If we break down this excitatory and inhibitory design we can find this is only one block with Groups=2 convolution, and add some operations in the output of this group=2 block. I think it is not easy to say it is inspired by biology pathways since all of them are fully learnable. 

- Logical operations do not always ensure identity mapping. Thus, I could not understand why it can train deep neural networks. Besides, a very important baseline is missing, i.e. Figure2(e). Can authors provide this result with right implementation?

Clarity: High

Novelty: Fair
Reproducibility: Code is provided in supplemental.
